module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Basic
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.UnitInterval
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Pi
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Prod
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Digraph.Basic
public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Combinatorics.LimitObjects.Graphon

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory MeasureTheory.Measure Finset

namespace LimitObjects

/--
A **tournamenton** is a measurable function `W : [0, 1] × [0, 1] → [0, 1]` satisfying the
tournament condition `W(x, y) + W(y, x) = 1`.
-/
structure Tournamenton where
  toFun : UnitInterval × UnitInterval → UnitInterval
  measurable : Measurable toFun
  tournament : ∀ x y : UnitInterval, (toFun (x, y) : ℝ) + (toFun (y, x) : ℝ) = 1

instance : CoeFun Tournamenton (fun _ => UnitInterval × UnitInterval → UnitInterval) := ⟨Tournamenton.toFun⟩

namespace Tournamenton

/-- Extensionality principle for `Tournamenton`. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {W₁ W₂ : Tournamenton} (h : ∀ p, W₁ p = W₂ p) : W₁ = W₂ := by
  cases W₁; cases W₂; congr; funext p; exact h p

end Tournamenton

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- The directed edge finset of a finite digraph. -/
def digraphEdgeFinset (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj] : Finset (V × V) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun p => D.Adj p.1 p.2)

/--
The integrand for the homomorphism density $t_{\vec{T}}(W)$ of a digraph $D$
in a tournamenton $W$ given a configuration `x : V → [0, 1]`.
-/
def tournamentonHomIntegrand (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj]
    (W : Tournamenton) (x : V → UnitInterval) : ℝ :=
  ∏ p ∈ digraphEdgeFinset D, (W (x p.1, x p.2) : ℝ)

/--
The **homomorphism density** $t_{\vec{T}}(W)$ of a digraph $D$ in a tournamenton $W$
on $[0, 1]$ equipped with the Lebesgue measure `volume`.
-/
noncomputable def tournamentonHomDensity (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj]
    (W : Tournamenton) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : V → UnitInterval, tournamentonHomIntegrand D W x ∂(Measure.pi fun _ => volume)

end LimitObjects

findings.description: The definition accepts arbitrary Mathlib digraphs, including loops and antiparallel arcs, but the edge-product integral is the tournament-limit homomorphism density only for oriented input graphs. Lean checks show that the one-vertex loop has density 1/2 in every Tournamenton, and the loop-free digon has density 1/4 in the constant-1/2 Tournamenton. Both digraphs have homomorphism density zero in every finite tournament and every tournament limit. Thus the unrestricted domain gives mathematically incorrect densities. The current tree-conjecture use is unaffected because D.IsOrientation T excludes both configurations.
findings.source_evidence: Thörnblad, Decomposition of tournament limits, §2 defines t(F,W) as the probability that F is contained in the sampled digraph. Theorem 4.1 characterizes tournament limits by zero loop and double-edge probabilities; Lemma 4.3 supplies the edge-product formula for tournament inputs. https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04271, LaTeX files master_preliminaries.tex and master_kernels.tex. Fox–Himwich–Mani–Zhou explicitly restrict their digraphs to orientations without self-loops or antiparallel edges: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08418, Introduction, remark preceding the tournament anti-Sidorenko definition. Mathlib.Combinatorics.Digraph.Basic explicitly allows self-loops and arbitrary adjacency relations.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restrict the input to oriented digraphs by requiring asymmetric adjacency, i.e. ∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u, or retain arbitrary digraphs and return zero when this condition fails. Update tournamentonHomIntegrand consistently. Irreflexivity alone is insufficient because antiparallel arcs also cause the error.

findings.description: The same missing oriented-input restriction occurs in this exported helper. Its product treats opposite arcs as independent requirements, contributing W(x_u,x_v)·W(x_v,x_u), although their joint occurrence in a tournament is impossible. A loop contributes W(x_v,x_v)=1/2 rather than zero. Consequently it is not the claimed homomorphism-density integrand for every permitted Digraph D; for the constant-1/2 kernel the digon integrand is identically 1/4 rather than zero.
findings.source_evidence: Thörnblad, https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04271, §2 specifies joint edge probabilities for each unordered vertex pair, with a separate loop probability. Theorem 4.1 requires the double-edge and loop probabilities to vanish for tournament limits. Chen–Clemen–Noel, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14138, Introduction, defines the input oriented graphs as having no self-loops and at most one arc between each pair of distinct vertices.
findings.suggested_fix: Require asymmetric adjacency for D, matching the intended oriented-graph domain, or define the integrand to be zero whenever D contains a loop or an antiparallel pair. Keep digraphEdgeFinset unchanged: it correctly lists all edges of a Mathlib digraph.

reformulations.difference: Uses measurable representatives satisfying W(x,y)+W(y,x)=1 everywhere, whereas Thörnblad's tournament-kernel definition requires this identity only almost everywhere.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is a choice of representatives for the same tournament limits, not literal equality of the sets of functions. Given an a.e.-measurable kernel f, choose a measurable representative g and set W(x,y)=(g(x,y)+1-g(y,x))/2. This is [0,1]-valued, satisfies the identity everywhere, and equals f a.e. I proved AECondition f ↔ ∃ W : Tournamenton, f =ᵐ W. I also proved that a.e. replacement preserves the edge-product density for loop-free digraphs, hence that universally quantified density bounds are equivalent under the two conventions. The sole downstream use supplies IsOrientation and is therefore within this domain.

reformulations.difference: Uses an inequality for every tournamenton instead of the source's inequality for every finite tournament.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed oriented D, every tournamenton is the limit of finite sampled tournaments, with their D-homomorphism densities converging to the displayed integral. Thus the finite inequality implies the tournamenton inequality. Conversely, encode an n-vertex tournament G by n equal-measure blocks, use its adjacency values between distinct blocks, and put 1/2 within blocks. Every homomorphism D→G contributes its full n^(-|V(D)|) to this tournamenton's density; other configurations contribute nonnegatively. Therefore t(D,G)≤t(D,W_G), and the tournamenton inequality implies the finite one. This equivalence holds for each orientation separately, preserving the order ∀ tree, ∃ orientation, ∀ host.

sources_consulted: Erik Thörnblad, Decomposition of tournament limits, §§2–4; abstract/version information https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04271 and LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/1604.04271.

Jacob Fox, Zoe Himwich, Nitya Mani, Yunkun Zhou, Variations on Sidorenko's conjecture in tournaments, Introduction and concluding remarks; https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08418 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2402.08418.

Hao Chen, Felix Christian Clemen, Jonathan A. Noel, On Tournament Anti-Sidorenko Orientations of Trees, abstract, Introduction, and bibliography; https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14138 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.14138.
Bibliographic lookup locating the arXiv version: https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejc.2017.07.023
Local Mathlib: Combinatorics/Digraph/Basic.lean and Orientation.lean; Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Acyclic.lean and Connectivity/Connected.lean.
Local Mathlib: MeasureTheory/Measure/MeasureSpaceDef.lean, Map.lean, AEMeasurable.lean, and QuasiMeasurePreserving.lean; MeasureTheory/Function/StronglyMeasurable/Basic.lean.
Historical calibration only: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md, pr04224.md, pr02295.md, pr04554.md, pr01220.md, and pr05007.md.
review.notes: The two findings are one underlying domain error affecting two exported declarations. No defect was found in the coercion, extensionality lemma, directed-edge finset, or the current downstream problem. Empty and edgeless inputs have density 1. All integrands were proved measurable, [0,1]-bounded, and integrable, ruling out Bochner-integral default-value problems. /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/representatives.lean both compile successfully; the checked counterexample and representative lemmas have no sorryAx dependency. No repository files were edited; pre-existing sandbox lakefile/run additions were left untouched.

submission.summary: Guarded the integrand by asymmetry of the adjacency relation, returning zero for digraphs with loops or antiparallel arcs. The density inherits this correction through its existing integral; the API and formula for oriented digraphs are unchanged. Updated both docstrings. The required module compilation and source-based regression tests pass without errors or warnings, and no sorry was introduced.

  toFun : UnitInterval × UnitInterval → UnitInterval
  measurable : Measurable toFun
  tournament : ∀ x y : UnitInterval, (toFun (x, y) : ℝ) + (toFun (y, x) : ℝ) = 1

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

def digraphEdgeFinset (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj] : Finset (V × V) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun p => D.Adj p.1 p.2)

/--
The integrand for the homomorphism density $t_{\vec{T}}(W)$ of a digraph $D$
in a tournamenton $W$ given a configuration `x : V → [0, 1]`.

This is the product over directed edges when `D` is oriented. It is zero if `D` has a loop
or antiparallel arcs, since such a digraph has no homomorphisms into a tournament.
-/
def tournamentonHomIntegrand (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj]
    (W : Tournamenton) (x : V → UnitInterval) : ℝ :=
  if ∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u then
    ∏ p ∈ digraphEdgeFinset D, (W (x p.1, x p.2) : ℝ)
  else 0

/--
The **homomorphism density** $t_{\vec{T}}(W)$ of a digraph $D$ in a tournamenton $W$
on $[0, 1]$ equipped with the Lebesgue measure `volume`.

It is zero if `D` has a loop or antiparallel arcs.
-/
noncomputable def tournamentonHomDensity (D : Digraph V) [DecidableRel D.Adj]
    (W : Tournamenton) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : V → UnitInterval, tournamentonHomIntegrand D W x ∂(Measure.pi fun _ => volume)

end LimitObjects
